4738575ced46c35d87c56b79fc130afada0b2222.summary: IBM Security X-Force describes Minodo, a backdoor loaded by the Dave Loader crypter since late February 2023. X-Force assesses its developers were linked to ITG14 (FIN7), and that former Trickbot/Conti (ITG23) members use it to deliver the Project Nemesis infostealer or Cobalt Strike. The report notes code overlap with the Lizar malware family. Attribution is hedged as assessment or likelihood.

hedges: The report says it was republished with the family renamed from Domino to Minodo to avoid confusion with the HCL Domino brand, and that the malware is unrelated to HCL.
X-Force assesses the Minodo malware was created by developers associated with ITG14, and suspects it was created by current or former ITG14 developers.
Former ITG23 members are likely behind recent Dave Loader campaigns and probably collaborated with current or former ITG14 developers.
The report says C2 address overlap with ITG14 infrastructure is insufficient for attribution but is consistent with other evidence.
Attribution of the Dave-loaded Cobalt Strike samples to Royal is described as suspected.
X-Force assesses that infostealers may often be deployed during lower priority infections.
X-Force assesses that ITG14 members responsible for developing Minodo probably had a relationship with Project Nemesis.

477096318b2545e6e1330383ccf77393d2a4378b.summary: SecurityScorecard's report, citing an FBI statement, attributes the May 2021 Colonial Pipeline ransomware attack to the DarkSide group, also called Carbon Spider, with moderate confidence. Its NetFlow analysis found over 80GB exfiltrated from Colonial on 6 May 2021, likely for extortion, with no direct disruption of pipeline operations. It also lists suspected other victims and says attribution analysis is still in progress.

hedges: SecurityScorecard can confirm with moderate confidence that DarkSide also known as Carbon Spider was responsible for the Colonial Pipeline attack, and describes the investigation as ongoing.
The report says attribution is often difficult; its analysis of competing hypotheses is marked in progress, and it calls Carbon Spider the most likely scenario.
No direct disruption of Colonial's critical infrastructure was found; it is only plausible that DarkSide damaged other parts of the network.
NetFlow data shows connections and volumes but not content, so the report could not view the exfiltrated data and assumes it will be used for extortion.
Other victims are suspected from NetFlow analysis only; some IP addresses may be attacker reviewers or proxies, and the report suspects they may have been used by attackers.
